### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **25** documentable anchor(s).

**33** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6868514b1c73c5fb2f7e1112a4749f182825447d`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **42** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6868514b1c73c5fb2f7e1112a4749f182825447d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2e194e71b39aa8a51fec8197351a8bbf55e6c130` — the merge of head `2af8fd548e43ae089975dfdc45e7e74507e290ed` into base `6868514b1c73c5fb2f7e1112a4749f182825447d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2e194e71b39aa8a51fec8197351a8bbf55e6c130 && git checkout 2e194e71b39aa8a51fec8197351a8bbf55e6c130
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6868514b1c73c5fb2f7e1112a4749f182825447d 2af8fd548e43ae089975dfdc45e7e74507e290ed && git checkout -B drift-repro 6868514b1c73c5fb2f7e1112a4749f182825447d && git merge --no-ff 2af8fd548e43ae089975dfdc45e7e74507e290ed

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6868514b1c73c5fb2f7e1112a4749f182825447d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6868514b1c73c5fb2f7e1112a4749f182825447d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bc90a53af6d439985c6d9185e7d52dd9d399aab6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/admin-standing-surface.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/bootstrap-platform-admin.ts, Head reviewed is the one the brief named; it had not moved (`gh api …/pulls/24373` → `head.sha` = `bc90a53a…`, 23 files, +909/−156, open against `main`). Rendered by an isolated at-tier reviewer subagent of the epic seat, from the card body and all nine comments, ADR-0131 D5/D10 on `origin/main`, plan 6251466182 rows 8b-0a and 8c-2, the PR body, the net diff `origin/main...bc90a53a`, and the head's 40 check-runs. The only commands run were `gh api` reads, `git fetch`/`git show`/`git diff` on the fetched refs, and the brief-prescribed `node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` (and its `--paths`/`--face` form from the `origin/main` copy, to read the face and `Scope:` floor). Nothing was built, tested or re-gated.

**Check-runs on the head: 40, all `completed`; 34 `success`, 6 `skipped` (the path-filtered Dogfood matrix shard, Build Docs, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke), 0 failure, 0 pending.** `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check:adr-0087-registration`), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, both single-writer guards and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` are green. They are green against the declaration as written (`Clause-②: no`, three `patch`), which is self-consistent and asks the ADR-0087 gate nothing; see ② for why that declaration is wrong.

**Face.** `reviewFace` on the 23 paths returns no `schema` and no `rules` hit (no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path), so `hits` is empty and the changeset's `Clause-②:` line decides between the narrowing and the declaration face. As committed (`no`, no arm) it reads the declaration face; as this record judges it must read (`(narrowing)` arm), the narrowing face, whose `Scope:` floor is every path of the diff outside the prose faces. Plan 6251466182 assigns 8b-0a to `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` by name ("platform standing"). `Scope:` above therefore lists every code path of the diff, the changeset, and the files the hunks make claims about.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding` — right on D5, one derivation site, four spellings of the predicate; the widening it performs is bounded but real.**

- `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:912-920`: `walled → false`; else `owner === null || (defaultOrganizationId !== undefined && owner === defaultOrganizationId)`. Read at exactly one place (:1497-1510, the §6 grant leg): the posture from `postureEnforcesWall(resolveTenancyPosture())` as before, the Default Organization from `readDefaultOrganizationId` (:934-942). Under a wall nothing anchors and `sys_organization` is never read (pinned, `resolve-authz-context.platform-admin-config.test.ts`: "a WALLED rig … does not ask which one it is"). This is D5's text: the `single` promotion row "owned by the Default Organization", the walled posture "no grant row … (unchanged)" plus the #11663 L5 retirement, and the organization-less row "until … D10's migration … clears it". **Right.**
- The anchoring grant applies in every organization (:1508-1510, `grantAppliesInTenant(...) || anchorsPlatformStanding(r)`), as the organization-less row always did (`grantAppliesInTenant(null, …)` is `true`). A deactivated `admin_full_access` still confers nothing: `take(body, active)` and the `&& active` at :1602. Any other organization's grant confers the set, never the rung (pinned). **Right.**
- **One code path with a posture parameter (the card's Constraint):** the DERIVATION of standing is one site, `resolve-authz-context.ts` §6, with `{ walled, defaultOrganizationId }` as its parameter. **Met.** But the PREDICATE now has four spellings: core :912-920, `bootstrap-platform-admin.ts:585-587` (`isAnchorHumanHolder`), `last-admin-guard.ts:1017-1031` (`anchorOwnerTest`), `ensure-default-organization.ts:505-512` (the `[null, defaultOrgId]` loop). That is the same count as before the PR (four `!organization_id` spellings), kept module-private on purpose so no package surface changes. Nothing but tests pins the four to each other. Not a defect of this PR; it is a lockstep-edit risk for 8c-2, when the `null` arm retires in all four at once — flag (③).
- **Can a caller-reachable write produce a Default-Organization `admin_full_access` grant for someone who should not hold platform standing?** Writers of `sys_user_permission_set`: (i) system writers — this promotion (:1108-1116) and the D10 ceremony (`organization-ownership-inventory.ts:567` fate `attribution`, `organization-ownership-plan.ts:1193-1209` via `default-organization`) — both by design; (ii) a platform admin through Setup CRUD (`admin_full_access` `'*'` allows create) — already PLATFORM_ADMIN; (iii) `organization_admin` and its wall-less `organization_admin_no_bypass` derivative: `sys_user_permission_set: { allowCreate: false, allowEdit: false, allowDelete: false }` (`default-permission-sets.ts:475`; `deriveWallLessOrgAdmin` copies everything but the superuser bits) — denied; (iv) **the DelegatedAdminGate** (`delegated-admin-gate.ts:799-828`): a delegated scope with `manageAssignments` whose `assignablePermissionSets` lists `admin_full_access` writes a grant row under the caller's context, and under `single` that row lands owned by the caller's organization — the Default Organization. A scope's assignable list is bounded by its outer scope (:876-905) and the root scope is a platform admin's authoring, so the authority chain is a platform admin's own decision to let someone hand out `admin_full_access`. On base such a row conferred the set (`'*'`, `modifyAllRecords`) without the rung; on this head it confers PLATFORM_ADMIN. The dev's "writing needs `modifyAllRecords`" is therefore not the whole answer — the delegated path exists — but it is bounded to platform-admin-authored authority and, under D3 ("under `single` the organization is the environment"), handing out `admin_full_access` in the Default Organization already was handing out the environment's superuser. **Judgment: accept-set widening on the permission boundary, bounded, acceptable in substance — and it must be declared as a widening (②).** The same holds for any pre-existing `admin_full_access` grant a 17.x platform admin wrote scoped to the Default Organization: it gains the rung on upgrade.

**(b) The Default Organization definition — seven copies, all agree, no reachable topology makes them disagree.**

Read: core `readDefaultOrganizationId` (:934-942), the guard's `readDefaultOrganizationId` (`last-admin-guard.ts:973-1006`), plugin-security `resolveDefaultOrganizationId` (`suggested-audience-bindings.ts:549-558`, what the promotion resolves through, :713-720/:807), plugin-auth `resolveDefaultOrgId` (`tenancy-service.ts:225-231`), `ensureDefaultOrganizationExists` (`default-organization-invariant.ts:87-93`), `findDefaultOrganizationId` (`ensure-default-organization.ts:341-346`), and the ceremony plan (`organization-ownership-plan.ts:446-451`, `:493`). Every one: `slug = 'default'` (exact; the slug carries a global unique index, `sys-organization.object.ts:465`, so at most one row), else the row when exactly one exists (`limit 2`, `length === 1`), else none. `sys_organization` has no soft-delete or status column, so "the only organization" cannot diverge on a hidden row. On every topology (0 / 1 / several-with-`default` / several-without) they answer alike. They differ only in what a FAILED read does: core `tryFind` throws `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` on an unreachable store and answers `[]` on an unprovisioned table; plugin-security's throws and `readPromotionGrantOwner` catches to `undefined` → promotion withheld with the `(or the read was refused)` wording; `tenancy-service` folds to `null`; the invariant propagates. On a reachable, provisioned store they agree. The guard's copy reads the Default Organization as the pending write would leave it (by design: a slug change or delete is judged on the after-image). **Right.** Consolidation is deferred on layering (core cannot import plugins) — flag for 8c-2 (③).

**(c) The A3 fix — right; pinned against the ceremony's output SHAPE, not against the ceremony.**

The ceremony attributes a `single` database's organization-less `sys_user_permission_set` rows to the Default Organization with no exemption for the promoted admin's grant (`organization-ownership-inventory.ts:567`, anchors `[]`; `organization-ownership-plan.ts:1193-1209`). On base the resolver read `!ownGrant` only and the holder scan asked `organization_id: null` only, so after `--apply` the admin lost PLATFORM_ADMIN and the next boot promoted again. On this head the resolver anchors the attributed row (the `[ADR-0131 D5]` suite), and the holder scan's leg A asks both owners (`bootstrap-platform-admin.ts:607-618`), so "an upgraded database … promotes nobody else" (fresh-boot golden) — a user holding both rows is one holder, the lower `id` answering (:616). **The fix is right.** The pin, however, inserts `organization_id: 'org_default'` by hand; the cli acceptance fixture (`organization-ownership-apply.test.ts`) is not extended with an admin grant, and the dev's A3 reading came from a deleted scratch copy. The equivalence rests on (b) — the ceremony plan and the readers sharing one definition — which this record verified by reading, not by a pinned run. Flag, non-blocking (③).

**(d) Cost of `readDefaultOrganizationId` on the authorization path.**

Resolver: runs once per `resolveUserAuthzGrants`, after Leg 1, only when `!walled` AND the principal holds an active `admin_full_access` grant with a non-null owner (:1498-1502). One indexed read when a `default`-slugged organization exists (the normal post-PR `single` deployment), two otherwise. Deduplicated within a request by `withRequestGrantsMemo`; the cross-request grants cache is off by default (`OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS=0`). So the promoted administrator pays one extra small read per uncached request under `single`; every other principal pays nothing; the batch-equivalence goldens are unchanged because their fixture holds the organization-less row (the PR's sentence is true of that fixture, not of a post-D5 admin). Guard: `anchorOwnerTest` adds one or two `sys_organization` reads per enumeration whenever any `admin_full_access` grant names an owner (always, post-PR, under `single`), and `enforceStanding` enumerates two or three times per guarded write plus the emptied-vs-fresh and dangling reads (`:1098`, `:1295`, `:1327`) — about three to six extra small reads per write on `sys_user`/`sys_member`/`sys_user_permission_set`/the activation ledger/`sys_organization`. Writes are rare and already pay comparable reads. **Acceptable; un-stated in the PR and changeset, and should be.**

**Other accept-set and permission changes, each named:**

- **Promotion withheld when no Default Organization is named** (`bootstrap-platform-admin.ts:1091-1107`: `error` line, `reason: 'default_organization_unresolved'`, no insert). Right under D5 (no NULL row) and D10 fate 4 (never a guessed owner). It IS a narrowing from base, and the topology is live: `auth-plugin.ts:850-855` only `warn`s on `ambiguous` and the boot proceeds; the tenancy census reports it at `error` with the two remedies. **Right in behaviour; wrong in declaration (②).**
- **Holder scan leg A asks two owners, ordered by `id`, lowest wins** (:607-618); legs B and C apply the same predicate. Deterministic. **Right.**
- **`bootstrapPlatformAdmin`'s return**: `reason?: string` (:732) — a new value is not a type-surface change; the PR body's claim holds. **Right.**
- **Last-admin guard** (`last-admin-guard.ts`): the enumeration (:1098-1121), the emptied-vs-fresh evidence (:1295-1296) and the switched-off-set read (:1327-1340) now count the Default Organization's grant; `beforeUpdate` on `slug` and `beforeDelete` on `sys_organization` at priority 20 (:1768-1781, :1833-1842), judged on the after-image, with `id` excluded as a non-standing key. Controls pinned (another organization's grant; a sole organization's slug or name change). **Right.** One write that moves the anchor is NOT hooked: an INSERT of a second organization while the sole organization is not slugged `default` (see ③).
- **`admin-standing-surface.ts:154-167`**: `sys_organization` as `derives`, columns `id`, `slug`; the f8eb73601 correspondence gate is green on it. **Right.**
- **`ensureDefaultOrganization` step 4** (`:557-560`): under `single`, reuse by the invariant's definition (a sole organization of any slug); under a wall only `slug='default'`, as before. Right — `tenancy-service.resolveDefaultOrgId` already bound users by that definition, and a second `default`-slugged organization would have BECOME the Default Organization and moved the anchor off the promoted grant. The golden move (`grant-readers-by-name.golden.test.ts` SINGLE owners `['usr_admin']` → `['usr_admin','usr_orgadmin']`) is recorded in the file. **Right in behaviour; a narrowing to declare (②).**
- **Walled posture**: `defaultOrganizationId` is `undefined` under a wall at every site (`:807`; core :1498; guard `:1025`; plugin-auth `:468-469`), so the walled branch reads, writes and refuses exactly as on base. **Unchanged, as the PR says.**
- **Cloud's legacy row**: cloud confers tenant-owner standing by writing the organization-less `admin_full_access` row (card comment 5521222826). That row still anchors under `single` here, so this PR does not lock cloud environment owners out; its retirement is 8c-2's and stays behind cloud's anchor move (#11977). **Right.**

### ② Semver level

**The declaration is wrong, on the PR and on the changeset, and so are the bumps.** Three narrowings and one widening ship under `Clause-②: no` with `"@objectstack/core": patch`, `"@objectstack/plugin-security": patch`, `"@objectstack/plugin-auth": patch` (`.changeset/11979-default-org-admin-grant.md:2-4`, `:9`; PR body line 3 `Clause-②: no` and the "Acceptance notes" bullet "Clause-②: no. No spec, REST answer or package entry changes…"). AGENTS.md:1088: "`(narrowing)` is BREAKING"; :1089-1090: a breaking changeset "must state the FROM → TO mapping and the one-line fix"; :1099-1100: "A breaking changeset must also state its ADR-0087 disposition, in writing"; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs:74-79`: in the launch window a breaking change ships as `minor`; `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:631` reads the `(narrowing)` arm as the breaking signal and will then demand the marker. The gates are green today only because the arm is absent — the exact hole #16421 closed.

The narrowings the diff performs:

1. **plugin-security** — FROM: a `single` deployment holding several organizations with none slugged `default` promoted its first user with an organization-less `admin_full_access` grant. TO: not promoted; one `error` line; `reason: 'default_organization_unresolved'`; no grant row written. Remedy: give the intended organization the slug `default` (or merge down to one organization, or declare a walled posture) — the next `kernel:ready` / sign-up pass promotes.
2. **plugin-auth** — FROM: a `sys_organization` `slug` change or delete was never refused. TO: refused (`PERMISSION_DENIED`, 403) when the row is the Default Organization whose `admin_full_access` grant is the last unbanned administrator's anchor. Remedy: grant another account administrator standing first (the refusal says so).
3. **plugin-auth** — FROM: `ensureDefaultOrganization` under `single` with a sole organization of another slug created a second, `default`-slugged organization and bound the administrator there. TO: it reuses the sole organization; no second organization is created. Remedy: none needed; an install that wants a `default`-slugged organization beside its existing one re-slugs the existing one or creates it explicitly.

The widening (①a): FROM: under `single` only an organization-less `admin_full_access` grant conferred PLATFORM_ADMIN. TO: a grant owned by the Default Organization confers it too and applies in every organization; a pre-existing Default-Organization-scoped `admin_full_access` grant gains the rung on upgrade; `sys_organization` becomes a standing-deriving table. That is "放宽接受集" on a permission boundary — the same class plan 6251466182 graded `yes` for 8a's read-scope widening.

**Required text:**
- `.changeset/11979-default-org-admin-grant.md:9` — `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (both facts true; `clause2-line.mjs` reads both). If the seat reads the Default-Organization row as D5's REPLACEMENT of the organization-less row rather than a widening of the accept set, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the floor; `Clause-②: no` without the arm is wrong either way.
- `:2-4` — all three bumps `minor` (core carries the widening; plugin-security narrowing 1; plugin-auth narrowings 2 and 3).
- Body: a `**BREAKING** (an accept-set narrowing), shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention` line, the three `**FROM:**` / `**TO:**` pairs above with their one-line remedies, and the widening stated as such — the shape stock changesets `24062-authored-install-scope-project.md` and `24086-install-primitive-parses-manifest.md` use.
- The ADR-0087 disposition marker `pnpm check:adr-0087-registration` will demand once the arm is present: exactly one HTML-comment marker of the form `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) …` — the honest category here: no spec key, export, option, error code or stored shape is added, removed or renamed; the only stored-shape move (NULL → Default Organization on the grant row) is D10's ceremony, already the ledger's business under C3, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite. State the other categories closed on facts, as `24062` does (the packages publish; no ADR-0087 id is touched; nothing exported is retired).
- PR body line 3 and the "Acceptance notes" bullet: the same arm and the same wording; the sentence "No spec, REST answer or package entry changes" stays true and is not the Clause-② question.
- Plan 6251466182 row 8b-0a reads "Clause-②: no (the dev measures)": the measurement is `yes (narrowing)` (floor `no (narrowing)`); the seat updates the row.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Q1 (os-dev-report) — "every Default-Organization `admin_full_access` grant confers platform standing under `single`": NOT settled by D5's text alone; settled by D3 + D10 fate 3 together. Accept A.** D5 says the promotion's row is owned by the Default Organization and no NULL row is produced; it does not say the anchor is every such row. What settles it: D3 ("under `single` the organization is the environment"), and D10 fate 3, whose ceremony produces exactly this shape with no column to stamp, so an anchor that read a marker would mis-read every upgraded database. Option B would be a spec change the ADR does not ask for. The reachable widening is the DelegatedAdminGate path and pre-existing Default-Organization-scoped grants (①a), both bounded to a platform admin's own authoring, and under D3 both already held the environment's superuser set. Not escalated; the condition is that ② declares it.

**Q2 — a multi-organization `single` deployment with no `default` slug fails closed: settled by D5 + D10 fate 4 + D9 together, not by D5's "no NULL grant row" clause alone. Keep A.** D5 forbids the NULL row; D10 fate 4 forbids a guessed owner ("Never guessed"); D9 already refuses every derived-owner write on that topology, the boot only `warn`s (`auth-plugin.ts:850-855`) and the tenancy census reports it at `error` with two remedies. Option B contradicts D5 outright. The card's "⛔ never a zero-admin boot" was written for the healthy topology — one organization, which the invariant creates — and on the ambiguous topology the two records collide; ruling A on #18707 makes D5 govern.
